conviction_note: Q2 revenue (~$44m) and adj-EBITDA (-$8.5m) were pre-guided on 2026-06-08 so the print itself is nearly a non-event; the swing factor is the FY26 $195.0m reaffirm, and EDGAR shows no 8-K of any kind since 2026-07-14 - meaning neither August acquisition is significant enough to bridge an H2 that has to grow +28% over H1 off a +6% Q1-to-Q2 sequential, into a 104k-ADV float that ran +6.7% in five sessions on a product press release; sized just inside the 4.48% historical median because insiders bought $6.0m at $3.25 in July and today's spot is $3.33.

findings.finding: Gloo has filed no 8-K of any kind since 2026-07-14 - none for the Cedarstone definitive agreement (2026-08-05) and none for the completed Midwestern acquisition (2026-08-11) - so neither deal is a 'significant' acquisition under Reg S-X, leaving no disclosed inorganic bridge for the FY26 guide's implied H2 of $109.5m (FY $195.0m less Q1 $41.5m actual and Q2 $44.0m guided) against an H1 of $85.5m and a Q1-to-Q2 sequential of only +6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Five sell-side analysts carry a Strong Buy with an average PT of $13.20 against a $3.33 spot, and Benchmark raised to $15 after Q1 on 'yet another beat and raise' - if the H2 bridge were understood to be unsupported by an acquisition of any reportable size, those models and that PT dispersion would not survive; the market is reading two August M&A press releases as revenue adds when the filing record says they are below the significance threshold and Midwestern was only the purchase of a stake Gloo already consolidated.
findings.independence: Gloo's own press page dates the Midwestern release as 'Gloo to Acquire Remaining Stake in Tech Talent Powerhouse Midwestern' (2026-06-08), i.e. a minority buy-in rather than a new consolidated business - https://gloo.com/press/releases ; separately EDGAR full-text search for 2026-08-01 to 2026-09-09 returns only Form 4 / 13F / 13G documents for this CIK and no company periodic or current report.

findings.finding: Gloo's own applicant-tracking system (Rippling) shows literally zero open roles - 'There are currently no open roles. Come back later!' - checked today, for a company that must add roughly $24m of half-on-half revenue and reach adjusted-EBITDA profitability by fiscal Q4.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates a private-company ATS page and it appears in no filing, wire item or preview; if it were priced you would see the growth-ramp half of the FY26 story discounted in the PT distribution rather than a unanimous 5-of-5 Buy at 4x spot. Deliberately sized small and two-sided: a frozen headcount is supportive of the Q3-breakeven/Q4-profitability opex line even as it argues against the top-line ramp, so it is not a clean negative.
findings.independence: Third-party boards corroborate the near-zero count - Glassdoor lists 1 Gloo job and Indeed 1 - https://www.glassdoor.com/Jobs/Gloo-Jobs-E800367.htm

findings.finding: The +6.7% five-day run-in rests substantially on a 2026-09-08 product launch, Gloo Code, whose entire evidence is a preliminary in-house benchmark ('approximately 70% at half the cost' vs Gemini 3 Pro / Sonnet 5 / OpenAI 5.6 Luna) that the release itself caveats as preliminary and possibly not generalising, with no pricing, no customer count and no revenue attached, launched into a 500-developer hackathon one day before the print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced in the wrong direction: the baseline shows run_up_5d of +6.73% while run_up_20d is -3.76%, i.e. the entire move is the last week, and Thrivent's Form 4 prints on 2026-09-02/03/04 were struck at $3.06-$3.12 against today's $3.33. On a name with 104k shares of 20-day average volume, a monetisation-free press release cannot survive a print that merely delivers the pre-guided $44m; a market that had priced the launch as a non-event would not have paid up 6.7% for it.
findings.independence: Gloo's own newsroom dates the release 2026-09-08 and shows no other company news between 2026-08-26 and the print - https://gloo.com/press/releases

findings.finding: Thrivent Financial for Lutherans, a 10% holder, has been selling GLOO Class A in the open market on essentially every trading day since late July - 4,243,600 shares held on 2026-07-29 down to 4,104,000 on 2026-09-04 - roughly 140k shares in five weeks, about 5% of daily volume, and the residual 4.10m shares is around 22% of the ~18.4m Class A shares outstanding (11.4m at 2026-04-30 plus the 7.0m July offering).
findings.why_not_priced: The individual Form 4s are 500-5,500 share dispositions that no screen flags and that news aggregators write up as trivia; the cumulative programme is only visible by differencing the post-transaction balances across nine filings. If the overhang were priced, the Class A float here is small enough that you would see it in a persistently wider quoted spread and in the stock failing to hold the $3.25 July deal price - instead it is sitting eight cents above it.
findings.independence: The earlier filing in the same series shows the 4,243,600 starting balance on 2026-07-29 - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2069785/000092963826002852/form4.xml - same source cluster as the finding above, so treat the two URLs as one document set.

findings.finding: Directors including CEO Scott Beck and Pat Gelsinger bought approximately $6.0m of the July follow-on at $3.25, and the stock closed today at $3.33 - the last hard-dollar insider mark on this equity is essentially today's price, set four weeks after the Q1 guide was given.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced - it is two months old and in the wire - which is exactly why it is sized at only +1.0 and is here to bound the downside rather than to generate it: it says the FY26 guide was underwritten with insider cash at a price the stock has not left, so a routine in-line print is unlikely to produce a 1990s-style collapse. Named explicitly so the set is not read as one-directional.

searched_and_found_nothing: Any Q2 pre-announcement - Gloo pre-announced Q4 FY25 on 2026-03-02 but issued no preliminary Q2 FY26 figure, so there is no second data point to trade against the 2026-06-08 guide
Any short-seller or activist report on GLOO - none exists that I could find
Any analyst downgrade, estimate cut or negative initiation since the Q1 print; coverage is 5 analysts, 5 Buys, average PT $13.20 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/gloo/forecast/)
Cedarstone's revenue or purchase price - financial terms were not disclosed and no 8-K or S-4 exists to size it

Whether the going-concern paragraph will be repeated or removed in the Q2 10-Q; with ~$33.2m cash at 2026-04-30, ~$17.1m of Q1 operating burn and ~$21m net raised in July, removal is genuinely possible and would be a positive - I could not resolve it either way, so it is in neither direction of the number
Third-party web-traffic or paid-user data for studio.ai.gloo.com - not obtainable

App-store review-volume trend as a demand proxy - a review aggregator cites a 2.3-star iPhone rating (https://aichief.com/ai-religion-tools/gloo/) but the consumer app is not where the revenue is, so I dropped it rather than dress it up
Whether the July underwriters' 1,050,000-share overallotment was exercised
Any customer loss, contract cancellation or denominational partner defection since 2026-06-08
baseline_tension: The baseline's warning that the four 8-K item-2.02 events are 'not earnings' is wrong and I am contradicting it: the 2025-12-17 (Q3 FY25), 2026-03-02 (preliminary Q4 FY25), 2026-04-14 (Q4/FY25) and 2026-06-08 (Q1 FY26) filings are all genuine company financial disclosures - the 55-day median gap is an artefact of the company pre-announcing Q4 on 2026-03-02 and confirming it on 2026-04-14, not of a phantom cadence - so the 1-up/3-down record and the 4.48% median magnitude ARE a usable base rate, and my negative number agrees with it rather than beating it; with no option chain there is no skew to cut against, the 20-day run-up is slightly negative while the 5-day is sharply positive, and it is that one-week run-in on a monetisation-free press release, not the drawdown, that my findings argue with.
